les: Hoe ons weet hoe hulle geleef het
kaps_punt: Hoe ons inligting van jagter-versamelaars en herders verkry: Stories, Voorwerpe, Rotstekeninge, Boeke, Tans (Vir die huidige sal ons oor hulle uitvind deur die waarneming van die lewende samelewings - etnografie)

items.bewering: Die jagter-versamelaars en herders het nie boeke geskryf of foto's geneem nie.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'The San' (https://sahistory.org.za/article/san): no recorded history of their own, knowledge comes from oral history and archaeology; the written /Xam record was made by others (W.H.I. Bleek and Lucy Lloyd, 1870s; https://lloydbleekcollection.cs.uct.ac.za). Holds for the period of these communities' traditional ways of life before colonial contact, which is how the lesson frames it.

items.bewering: Historici en argeoloë gebruik daarom ander leidrade, wat ons bronne noem.
items.bron: South African History Online (https://sahistory.org.za/article/san; https://sahistory.org.za/node/65017): the evidence used is archaeological remains, rock art, oral tradition and later colonial writings.

items.bewering: Bronne as 'leidrade' (vergelyking: om die verlede uit te vind soos wat 'n mens met leidrade 'n antwoord vind)
items.bron: Mapping checked: a clue is partial evidence that must be interpreted and combined with others to reach an answer, which is how historical and archaeological sources are used (see the multi-source approach in https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:c83240db-c713-425e-98cd-227d605d38ba and in rock-art research, https://www.bradshawfoundation.com/south_africa/san_rock_art/). The lesson itself closes the obvious gap a learner might reason into ('Elke bron is net een leidraad'), so the comparison does not imply that one source gives the whole answer.

items.bewering: Party stories is oor baie geslagte heen oorvertel, van ouers na kinders.
items.bron: South African History Online (https://sahistory.org.za/article/san): the San have a rich oral history passed down across generations; Bleek and Lloyd recorded stories from /Xam narrators such as //Kabbo who had learned them orally (https://lloydbleekcollection.cs.uct.ac.za; https://www.capetownmuseum.org.za/they-built-this-city/kabbo).

items.bewering: Die stories vertel onder meer van diere en van wat mense geglo het.
items.bron: Recorded /Xam narratives centre on the Mantis (/Kaggen), the southern San trickster-deity, and animal characters (one scholar counts 73 animal species across Khoisan myths), and the Bleek-Lloyd material records customs and beliefs (Hollmann ed., Customs and Beliefs of the |Xam, https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/customs-and-beliefs-of-the-xam/foreword-to-the-second-edition/885D718CFF4D1A0DD2AF3BBC7EB4A5E8; https://talkingstories.uoregon.edu/?p=3457).

items.bewering: Voorwerpe (artefakte) is dinge wat mense self gemaak of verander het om te gebruik.
items.bron: Standard archaeological definition: an artefact is any object made or modified by people (New World Encyclopedia, 'Artifact (archaeology)', https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Artifact_(archaeology); Oxford Archeox fact sheet, https://archeox.conted.ox.ac.uk/fact-sheets/artefacts.html). 'Om te gebruik' fits tools and ornaments; it is a harmless narrowing at this level.

items.bewering: Argeoloë vind dit in die grond en in rotsskuilings.
items.bron: Excavated hunter-gatherer material from rock shelters in southern Africa, e.g. Little Muck Shelter, Limpopo (Southern African Field Archaeology, https://journals.uj.ac.za/index.php/safa/article/download/3061/1832/10536) and Sehonghong and Melikane rock shelters, Lesotho (https://news.umich.edu/stone-age-likes-study-establishes-eggshell-beads-exchanged-over-30000-years).

items.bewering: Klipgereedskap en krale van volstruiseierdop wys hoe mense gewerk en hulself versier het.
items.bron: Southern African Field Archaeology, Little Muck Shelter study (https://journals.uj.ac.za/index.php/safa/article/download/3061/1832/10536): foragers made worked stone and bone tools and produced ostrich eggshell beads for personal ornamentation, exchange and symbolism; OES beads in South Africa go back to Border Cave, about 44 000-41 000 years ago.

items.bewering: Rotskuns of rotstekeninge is kuns wat mense op rotse geverf of in die klip ingekap het.
items.bron: Southern African rock art has two forms: paintings, mostly in caves and shelters, and engravings, mostly pecked (some incised) into rock in the dry interior (Scientific American, 'Rock Art in Southern Africa', https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/rock-art-in-southern-africa-2005-01/; University of Pretoria repository, Smith 2004, https://repository.up.ac.za/bitstream/handle/2263/14121/Smith_Taking(2004).pdf). 'Ingekap' matches pecking.

items.bewering: Baie daarvan wys diere soos die eland en mense wat dans.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum of Art, 'San Ethnography' essay (https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/san-ethnography): the eland was the most commonly depicted animal in most areas, and depictions of healing or trance dances are ubiquitous; Bradshaw Foundation, San rock art of the Drakensberg (https://www.bradshawfoundation.com/south_africa/san_rock_art/).

items.bewering: Navorsers dink vandag dat baie van die kuns gaan oor wat die mense geglo het.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum essay (https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/san-ethnography): the emphasis on eland, which was not the main game eaten, reflects belief rather than diet; Lewis-Williams's widely held interpretation links much of the art to religious experience and trance (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lewis-Williams). Scholars still argue about WHICH beliefs (the shamanistic model is contested and refined, e.g. https://mdpi.com/2077-1444/12/12/1099), but not that much of the art relates to belief. The hedged wording ('dink', 'baie van') matches the evidence.

items.bewering: Baie later het mense van elders die San en die Khoikhoi ontmoet en oor hulle geskryf.
items.bron: South African History Online: Portuguese sailors met Khoikhoi herders at Mossel Bay in 1488 (Dias) and 1497 (Da Gama, whose voyage journal describes them) (https://www.sahistory.org.za/article/vasco-da-gamas-voyage-discovery-1497); Dutch settlement at the Cape from 1652 (https://sahistory.org.za/article/san). This is very recent compared with stone tools, ostrich eggshell beads and rock art tens of thousands of years old, so 'baie later' holds (although some rock art is itself recent).

items.bewering: Party het ook die San se stories neergeskryf.
items.bron: UCT Lloyd and Bleek Collection (https://lloydbleekcollection.cs.uct.ac.za): Wilhelm Bleek (born in Germany) and Lucy Lloyd recorded /Xam narratives in the 1870s, more than 12 000 pages; listed in UNESCO Memory of the World register in 1997.

items.bewering: Elke boek wys hoe sy skrywer die mense gesien het. Vra dus altyd wie 'n boek geskryf het en hoekom.
items.bron: Scholarship on the Bleek-Lloyd records notes that colonial-era collections reflect the recorders' choices as well as the original tellings (https://talkingstories.uoregon.edu/?p=3457; https://ajol.info/index.php/esarjo/article/view/30953). Standard source-criticism principle in history.

items.bewering: Navorsers leer ook deur mense wat vandag leef dop te hou en met hulle te praat. Hierdie soort navorsing noem ons etnografie.
items.bron: Ethnography: descriptive study of a society based on fieldwork, by participant observation supplemented by interviews (New World Encyclopedia, 'Ethnography', https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Ethnography; CUNY 'Understanding Ethnography', https://ethnographymadeeasy.commons.gc.cuny.edu/understanding-ethnography/). Kalahari San ethnography is used this way in rock-art research (Met essay above).

items.bewering: Leefwyses verander met die tyd, dus wys hierdie navorsing nie presies hoe mense destyds geleef het nie.
items.bron: Pargeter et al., 'Primordialism and the Pleistocene San of southern Africa', Antiquity 2016 (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/abs/primordialism-and-the-pleistocene-san-of-southern-africa/45D6E61597C34A496AB5A0B6FA1C7632); 'Analogy and the danger of oversimplifying the past', Antiquity (https://cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/abs/analogy-and-the-danger-of-oversimplifying-the-past/2F8A58B7145CB7D5B6EDEDF0B5CF61A0); the 1980s Kalahari Debate: present-day groups changed through contact and cannot be read straight back onto the past.

items.bewering: Elke bron is net een leidraad, en saam vertel die bronne ons die meeste.
items.bron: Comparative superlative about method, not a record claim. Combining independent kinds of evidence gives a fuller picture than any one (triangulation; https://ethnographymadeeasy.commons.gc.cuny.edu/understanding-ethnography/); San rock-art interpretation rests on exactly this combination of archaeology, the art and the Bleek-Lloyd and Kalahari ethnography (https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/san-ethnography). True as stated; no softening needed.

items.bewering: bronne: Dinge soos foto's, geskrifte, stories, onderhoude en voorwerpe wat vir ons iets van vandag en van lank gelede vertel.
items.bron: Consistent with standard historical usage of primary sources (documents, images, oral testimony, objects); South African History Online lists the same kinds of evidence for San and Khoikhoi history (https://sahistory.org.za/article/san). 'Van vandag' is correct for interviews and ethnographic observation.

items.bewering: leidraad: Iets wat jou help om die antwoord op 'n vraag uit te vind.
items.bron: Word sense checked against Wiktionary (leidraad, from leiden 'to guide' + draad 'thread', https://kaweah.freedombox.rocks/kiwix/wiktionary_en_all_maxi_2023-04/leidraad) and Afrikaans usage in Lexikos as 'an indication/pointer' (https://lexikos.journals.ac.za/pub/article/view/913/432). The WAT entry itself was behind a login and was not read; the clue sense used here is well attested in both sources.

items.bewering: historikus: Iemand wat bronne bestudeer om die verlede te verstaan en te beskryf.
items.bron: A historian studies and writes about the past using evidence (difference.wiki, 'Historian vs. Archaeologist', https://difference.wiki/historian-vs-archaeologist; university lecture notes, https://uomustansiriyah.edu.iq/media/lectures/8/8_2019_01_07!07_34_30_AM.pdf). Weak sources, but the definition is uncontroversial and does not wrongly limit historians to written sources.

items.bewering: argeoloog: Iemand wat dinge van lank gelede soek en ondersoek om uit te vind hoe mense geleef het.
items.bron: An archaeologist studies past human life through excavation of sites and analysis of material remains (CareerExplorer, https://www.careerexplorer.com/careers/archaeologist/; https://difference.wiki/historian-vs-archaeologist).

items.bewering: artefak: 'n Voorwerp wat mense self gemaak of verander het.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia, 'Artifact (archaeology)' (https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Artifact_(archaeology)): any object made or modified by a human culture, individual or group. Consistent with the study block.

items.bewering: rotskuns: Kuns wat mense op klip verf of in die klip inkap.
items.bron: Scientific American, 'Rock Art in Southern Africa' (https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/rock-art-in-southern-africa-2005-01/): paintings and pecked or incised engravings. Consistent with the study block.

items.bewering: etnografie: Navorsing waarin iemand mense dophou en met hulle praat om te leer hoe hulle leef.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia, 'Ethnography' (https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Ethnography); CUNY 'Understanding Ethnography' (https://ethnographymadeeasy.commons.gc.cuny.edu/understanding-ethnography/): observation of people in their everyday settings, supplemented by interviews. Consistent with the study block.

opsomming: All 24 claims are verified against museum, university, journal and South African History Online sources, including the one superlative ('saam vertel die bronne ons die meeste') and the clue comparison, whose mapping holds because the lesson itself says each source is only one clue; nothing needs changing, though a person may note that the meaning of San rock art is still debated in its detail, which the lesson's hedged 'navorsers dink' already reflects.
